-sS: TCP SYN scan (stealth scan, half-open connection)
-sT: TCP Connect scan (full connection, more visible in the target's logs than -sS)
-sU: Also scans UDP ports — takes much longer than a TCP scan
-sV: Attempts to identify the service version running on each port (sends extra probes)
-sC: Runs the default set of NSE scripts to pull extra info from services
-A: Aggressive mode (OS detection + version detection + script scan + traceroute) — high footprint, easy to detect
-O: Attempts to fingerprint the target's OS (more intrusive than a plain service scan)
-Pn: Skips host discovery (ping) and scans every IP as if it were always online — may increase scan time
-n: Skips DNS resolution, scans slightly faster
-F: Scans only the 100 most common ports (faster than scanning every port)
--open: Only shows ports found open in the results
-f: Splits packets into small fragments to evade basic firewalls/IDS that only inspect whole packets
--script: Runs the specified NSE script, which may send extra requests to the target depending on the script
-T0: Paranoid timing — very slow, best at avoiding IDS detection
-T1: Sneaky timing — slow, focused on evading detection
-T2: Polite timing — reduces load on the network and target
-T4: Aggressive timing — fast, suited to internal networks/labs, may trigger IDS alerts
-T5: Insane timing — fastest, high chance of missed results and detection
-v: Raises verbosity — shows real-time progress and detail during the scan
--version-all: Tries every service probe for the most thorough version identification (slower)
